solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crashing bus in front of Abbey Road is ludicrous

indicators.note: the scrambled bus letters go inside the other pieces
the front of Abbey is its opening letter
a crashing bus is wrecked, so its three letters are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A bus crashing outside the famous Abbey Road studios would be a ludicrous sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abbey Road' looks like one name, the famous London recording studio street, but the clue splits it so only Abbey's front letter is used. 'Crashing' scrambles the bus, and 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are plain synonyms describing something ridiculous or laughably unreasonable.

clue.text: Amateur's roguish manner drawing in master

definitions.note: the 's is 'is'; the definition is the adjective amateur, as in an armchair critic

indicators.note: the pair of words pulls a further letter into themselves, so it sits inside them

parts.note: arch means playfully roguish or mischievous
M is a common abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree's M
an air is a manner or bearing

explanation.surface: An amateur's rascally way of behaving manages to win over an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing in' pulls the master's letter into the joined pair, just after their first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An armchair critic or fan is one who comments from home without real experience, so the word describes an amateur.

clue.text: Maker of many films, at least forty including singular European

indicators.note: the first word takes another letter inside itself

parts.note: scores means two or more twenties, so forty or more
S is the grammar abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: Describes a prolific film-maker whose output tops forty, including a single European picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At least forty' is a clever way to say SCORES, since two or more scores make forty or more.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Scorsese is the American director of dozens of films, such as Taxi Driver and Goodfellas.

clue.text: After regular deprivations, Freudian's a wreck

indicators.note: losing letters at regular intervals leaves every other letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst is left a nervous wreck after being repeatedly deprived of something.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove F, E, D and A from FREUDIAN, every other letter, leaving the even-placed R, U, I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in ruins is a wreck, so the noun names a destroyed thing or state of collapse.

clue.text: Possible means of spreading poison or spleen, through phone mostly

indicators.note: the spleen word runs through the middle of the phone word, so it sits inside it
mostly means the phone word loses its last letter

parts.note: the blower is old British slang for the telephone
the pip is a fit of irritation or bad temper, as in 'it gives me the pip', so it means spleen

explanation.surface: Suggests poison or bile being passed along a telephone line, nearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blower' is dated British slang for a phone, and 'the pip' is British for a fit of annoyance. 'Mostly' drops the phone word's last letter; 'through' sets the spleen word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowpipe shoots poisoned darts, so it is one way to deliver poison to a target.

clue.text: Custom dentalware masks a state possibly requiring maxillofacial work

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cover and hide the state inside them
custom as in custom-made, the dental fittings refashioned into a new shape

parts.note: NJ is the postal abbreviation for New Jersey, a US state

explanation.surface: Bespoke dental fittings conceal a condition that could need jaw surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Custom' (as in custom-made) is the anagram signal; 'masks' hides the state's postal code within the rearranged letters. 'A state' looks like part of the definition but supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, prominent jaw is the kind of facial feature that maxillofacial (jaw and face) surgeons sometimes correct.

clue.text: What for energy must go into dairy product

indicators.note: the energy letter has to be placed within the other word

parts.note: 'what for?' asks why
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Asks why energy must be put into making a dairy food.
explanation.definitionFit: Whey is the watery liquid left after milk curdles in cheesemaking, a by-product of the dairy.

clue.text: Victim of global warming in current century, with rising speed?

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word reads from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: pace is speed

explanation.surface: Asks whether this century's rapid pace of change is what makes polar ice a victim of climate change.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'rising' means reading upwards, so the speed word is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice sheets are melting as the planet heats up, making them a prime casualty of climate change.

clue.text: Being led away from having the right variable

indicators.note: the word led is taken out of the longer word

parts.note: entitled means having a right to something
taken as written
Y is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: Someone is led away from a position of entitlement, all for one changing factor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' as a noun, a living thing, not the verb form it seems in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is any existing thing or creature, which is what this word means in philosophy.

clue.text: Short-termism is the author's one answer about work

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: the author's means my
OP is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A writer claims to have one answer concerning work: thinking only in the short term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' here is just a link meaning 'regarding'; the pieces are in clue order except that OP comes before I and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally short-sightedness, the word is used figuratively for a lack of foresight or long-term planning.

clue.text: Going down without son is rude

indicators.note: the son's letter is dropped from the phrase

parts.note: in descent means going down

explanation.surface: Coming down a slope without one's son would be a rude thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecent means offensive to good taste, especially sexually crude, which fits rude.

clue.text: Pessimist's repeated utterance after Madame blocks entry

definitions.note: the 's is 'is'; the definition is a gloomy person

indicators.note: the chant comes after the door piece
Madame stands in the way, filling the doorway

parts.note: a door is an entry
a chant is a phrase said over and over

explanation.surface: A gloomy soul repeats a catchphrase after a French lady stands in the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blocks' puts Madame's abbreviation inside the entry word, just before its last letter; 'after' places the chant at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who always predicts disaster is a gloom-monger, which is exactly this hyphenated noun.

clue.text: Even parts of The South turned calm

indicators.note: turned means the picked letters are read backwards
the even parts are the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Parts of the American South became peaceful.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of THE SOUTH are H, S, U, H; 'turned' reads them backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A hush is a quiet stillness, and as a verb it means to make calm or silent.

clue.text: Readies a bit of balm on eyes

indicators.note: only a piece of the phrase is used, the letters running across the words

explanation.surface: Someone prepares a little soothing ointment for tired eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Readies' looks like a verb, but it is British slang for cash: 'the readies'.
explanation.definitionFit: The readies is British slang for ready cash, so it is a synonym for notes and coins.

clue.text: Foolish rage, receding with time

indicators.note: receding means the craze word goes backwards

parts.note: a rage is a fad or craze, as in 'all the rage'

explanation.surface: A silly bout of anger fades as time passes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rage' seems to mean anger, but here it means a craze.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is an informal British word for silly or foolish.

clue.text: Issue patch with internal binary value flipped

indicators.note: the binary digit goes inside the other word
flipped means the patch word is turned backwards

parts.note: turf is one's patch or home territory
1, written as I, is one of the two binary digits

explanation.surface: Sounds like a software patch that flips an internal bit.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing surface hides the British sense of turf and patch as one's territory. 'Flipped' turns TURF into FRUT, and 'internal' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fruit of the womb means offspring, so fruit can mean issue or children.

clue.text: Confronted with unstimulating drink, got up

indicators.note: in a down entry, got up means the drink is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: decaf coffee has no caffeine to stimulate

explanation.surface: Someone faced with a dull caffeine-free coffee rose from the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Faced means met head on, a direct synonym for confronted.

clue.text: Helpful turn is somehow ridiculous

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: mental is slang for crazy or ridiculous

explanation.surface: A useful change of direction turns out to be ridiculous somehow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow' rearranges TURN IS into INSTRU.
explanation.definitionFit: Being instrumental in something means helping it happen, so the word means useful or helpful.

clue.text: Perhaps Dutch collector's gambit is scuppered

indicators.note: a scuppered plan is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A Netherlands art collector's opening ploy comes to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is old Cockney slang for a wife (from 'duchess'), so a collector of Dutches has several wives. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man with more than one wife at once collects wives, and wife is one sense of Dutch, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Matted lint clogs heckle but it goes fast

indicators.note: the tangled fluff blocks up the other word from inside

parts.note: to jeer is to heckle

indicators.note: matted fibres are tangled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Tangled fluff gets in the way of a heckler, but things move along fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matted' is the anagram signal, and 'clogs' puts the jumbled fluff inside the heckling word after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet airliner is a fast passenger aircraft.

clue.text: Realistic shooting's popular with them during hollow ceremony

indicators.note: the popular and them words fall within the hollow word

parts.note: a cave is a hollow
in means popular or fashionable
'em is the colloquial short form of them
a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Realistic filming finds favour with people at an empty ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow ceremony' looks like one phrase but gives two separate pieces. 'During' sets the popular and them words inside the hollow, after its first letter. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinéma vérité is a documentary film style aiming for naturalism, so its shooting is realistic.

clue.text: Map-makers following track's pitiable quality

indicators.note: the map-makers come after the track

parts.note: a path is a track; the 's is 'has' or a link
OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency

explanation.surface: Cartographers tracing a route find something pitiful about it.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is Ordnance Survey, Britain's official map-makers.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathos is the quality in art or life that stirs pity or sadness.

clue.text: Rag day organised to make sense of Orientation?

indicators.note: the letters are organised into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A student charity rag day is arranged to help people find their way around.
explanation.walkthrough: A rag day is a British student charity fundraising day. 'Orientation' means sexual orientation, not finding direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaydar is slang for a supposed knack of sensing someone's sexual orientation, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Now I see bachelor obsessed captain

parts.note: aha is the exclamation of sudden understanding
B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in a BA degree

explanation.surface: A sudden realisation that a single man is fixated on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain Ahab of Moby-Dick is fixated on hunting the white whale.

clue.text: Prison guard succeeded with gang

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in family trees
a crew is a gang

explanation.surface: A warder joined up with a criminal gang and did well.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is British prison slang for a warder or jailer.

clue.text: Arts graduate's going to Globe

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts; the 's here is 'is', working with 'going to'
's going to means will, shortened to 'll

explanation.surface: An arts graduate is heading off to the Globe Theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduate's going to' is 'graduate will', shortened to the contraction 'll.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is any round sphere, the same shape as a globe.

clue.text: Compressed mass is about kinetic energy

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means about
KE is the physics abbreviation for kinetic energy

explanation.surface: Sounds like a physics statement about compressed matter and its energy of motion.
explanation.definitionFit: A cake can be any solid block of pressed material, like a cake of soap.

clue.text: Stately edifice rising third

parts.note: in tonic sol-fa, doh up to me is a rising major third; do is the first note
me (or mi) is the third note of the scale, two steps above do

explanation.surface: A grand building goes up to its third storey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising third' is music: going from doh up to me in the sol-fa scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A dome is a large rounded roof, and by extension an imposing domed building.

clue.text: Refuge means getting behind hospital plan

indicators.note: the means word goes after the other pieces

parts.note: an idea is a plan
a way is a means of doing something

explanation.surface: A shelter is the only option after a hospital scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a secluded place to retreat to, a synonym for a refuge.

clue.text: Gesture to expose the rear (object to the rear being covered)

indicators.note: the reversed object word is wrapped by the other word

parts.note: to moon is to bare one's buttocks

indicators.note: the object word faces backwards

parts.note: it is an object, a thing

explanation.surface: A rude gesture of baring one's backside, with a coy aside about keeping things covered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To the rear' turns the object word round, and 'being covered' wraps the baring-the-backside verb around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion is a movement of the hand or body made to signal, a gesture.

clue.text: Italian town's medical department in endless misery

definitions.note: the 's is 'is'; the definition is the town

indicators.note: the department goes inside the misery word
the misery word loses its final letter

parts.note: sorrow is misery
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: An Italian town's hospital department is stuck in unending misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the final letter of the misery word, and 'in' sets ENT, the ear, nose and throat department, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorrento is a coastal town on the Bay of Naples in southern Italy.

clue.text: Pumpkin eater taking wife for a mug?

indicators.note: the name takes the extra letter inside it

parts.note: Peter Peter Pumpkin Eater is the nursery rhyme man who kept his wife in a pumpkin shell

explanation.surface: The nursery-rhyme pumpkin eater takes a wife, though she might be a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A mug' tempts as a fool, but pewter is the metal a mug is made of; the question mark marks the definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Pewter is a tin alloy traditionally used for drinking tankards, and the word can name such a tankard.
